message.content:
I need to find the Next.js/TypeScript source file(s) that define the admin portal's left sidebar navigation for the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon. From a screenshot, the sidebar currently has these top-level group headers and items, in this order:

- Overview (single item, no group header)
- CUSTOMERS: Clients, Support
- FLEET: Servers, Infrastructure, Operations, Domains
- REVENUE: Billing, Catalog, Promotions
- MARKETING: Marketing, Studio, Cold Email, Leads (partially visible, may have more items below)
- (likely more below, probably a SYSTEM group with items like Settings/System, possibly Docs, Board, etc. — not visible in the screenshot)

There's also an "ACCOUNT BALANCE" widget pinned near the bottom, and a "Collapse" toggle at the very bottom, suggesting there's already a collapse/expand mechanism for the WHOLE sidebar (not per-group). The user wants:
1. Group headers to become collapsible/expandable sections (each group like CUSTOMERS, FLEET, REVENUE, MARKETING, SYSTEM can individually collapse/expand, likely via a chevron/click on the header).
2. Reorganize the nav: give "Cold Email" its own top-level group/submenu (separate from MARKETING), move "Content" (probably an existing item, maybe under Marketing or elsewhere — check if there's a "Content" nav item anywhere, e.g. blog/CMS related) into the MARKETING group, give "Mail" its own submenu (look for an existing "Mail" or "Email" admin section, likely for the transactional/Mailcow admin UI, separate from Cold Email marketing tool), and rename "System" group header to "Settings".
3. Persist collapsed/expanded state per group across sessions (localStorage most likely, since this is client-side sidebar state, not something that needs to be per-admin-user in the DB necessarily — but check if there's precedent for user-preference persistence in this codebase already, e.g. a Settings/Preference model in Prisma, or existing localStorage usage patterns for UI state).

Please find and report back:
1. The exact file path(s) of the sidebar/nav component (search for strings like "ACCOUNT BALANCE", "Collapse", "CUSTOMERS", "FLEET", "Cold Email", "Catalog", "Promotions" in /opt/nxeon/app or /opt/nxeon/components etc.)
2. The full current structure of the nav config (the array/object defining groups and items) — full file contents or the relevant section, with line numbers.
3. Whether the sidebar is currently collapsible as a whole (single collapse button) or if any per-group collapse already exists, and how that state is currently stored (React state, localStorage, cookie, DB?).
4. Any existing "Content" nav item (blog/CMS/content management) and where it currently lives in the nav structure.
5. Any existing "Mail" or "Email" (non-cold-email, e.g. Mailcow/transactional mail admin) nav item and where it currently lives.
6. The full "SYSTEM" group contents (items under it) since it wasn't visible in the screenshot.
7. Any existing localStorage-based UI state persistence patterns elsewhere in the codebase I should follow for consistency (search for `localStorage` usage in admin components).

This is read-only research — do not edit any files. Report file paths and relevant code snippets so I can make the edit myself.

356	/** Every entry across every section, in sidebar order. */
357	export function adminEntries(): AdminEntry[] {
358	  return ADMIN_NAV.flatMap((g) => g.entries);
359	}

361	/**
362	 * Does `pathname` belong to `href`? Exact match, or a detail route beneath it
363	 * (`/admin/users/123`). The bare "/admin" only ever matches exactly so it can
364	 * never swallow every deeper route.
365	 */
366	export function hrefMatches(href: string, pathname: string): boolean {
367	  if (pathname === href) return true;
368	  if (href === "/admin") return false;
369	  return pathname.startsWith(href + "/");
370	}
371	
372	/**
373	 * Resolve which top-level entry owns a given admin pathname, by longest
374	 * matching member href. Returns null for admin paths outside the IA.
375	 */
376	export function entryForPath(pathname: string): AdminEntry | null {
377	  let best: { entry: AdminEntry; len: number } | null = null;
378	  for (const entry of adminEntries()) {
379	    for (const tab of entry.tabs) {
380	      if (hrefMatches(tab.href, pathname) && (!best || tab.href.length > best.len)) {
381	        best = { entry, len: tab.href.length };
382	      }
383	    }
384	  }
385	  return best?.entry ?? null;
386	}

I now have everything needed. Here's the full report. ## 1. File paths of the sidebar/nav components - **`/opt/nxeon/components/portal/Shell.tsx`** (839 lines) — the actual sidebar/rail renderer, shared by both the customer dashboard and admin portal. Contains "Account Balance" (line 625), the whole-sidebar "Collapse" toggle (lines 632–654), and the `localStorage` persistence for it (lines 248–261). - **`/opt/nxeon/lib/admin-groups.ts`** (387 lines) — the admin nav **data/IA config** (`ADMIN_NAV`). This is what you'll edit to reorganize groups/entries. - **`/opt/nxeon/app/admin/layout.tsx`** — server component that reads `ADMIN_NAV`, filters it by feature flags/RBAC, computes badge roll-ups, and maps it into the generic `NavSection[]` shape `Shell` expects. - **`/opt/nxeon/components/admin/SubTabs.tsx`** — renders the horizontal sub-tab pill bar for a multi-member entry (the `` mounted once in the admin layout, and the underlying ``). Note: none of "CUSTOMERS", "FLEET", "Catalog" as literal grep hits turned up directly in Shell.tsx (Shell.tsx is generic and just renders `section.label`/`item.label` from props) — the actual group labels ("Customers", "Fleet", "Revenue", etc.) live only in `lib/admin-groups.ts`. ## 2. Full current nav config (`/opt/nxeon/lib/admin-groups.ts`) Read in full above; key structural facts: - `ADMIN_NAV: AdminGroup[]` — array of groups, each `{ key, label?, entries: AdminEntry[] }`. - Each `AdminEntry` is `{ key, label, icon, tabs: SubTabItem[] }`. The sidebar shows **one row per entry** (`tabs[0]` is the landing href); `tabs[1..]` become the horizontal sub-tab bar on the page, not sidebar sub-items. There is **no nested/expandable sidebar tree today** — that's an important constraint for your "per-group collapse" plan, since collapsing currently only makes sense at the **group** level (the `

{section.label}

` headers), not per-entry. Current groups, in order (line numbers from the file above): 1. `start` (no label) → Overview (line 46-63) 2. `customers` label "Customers" (64-88) → Clients, Support 3. `fleet` label "Fleet" (89-135) → Servers, Infrastructure, Operations, Domains 4. `revenue` label "Revenue" (136-174) → Billing, Catalog, Promotions 5. `marketing` label "Marketing" (175-263) → Marketing, Studio, **Cold Email, Leads, Campaigns, Sending identity, Deliverability, Suppression** (the last six are the exploded Cold Email entries, all still inside the `marketing` group) 6. `agency` label "Agency" (264-281) → Sitewave (feature-flag gated, hidden unless `feature_admin_agency` setting is on) 7. `ads` label "Ads" (282-298) → Adloop (feature-flag gated, `feature_admin_ads`) 8. `platform` label "Platform" (299-353) → **Content, Mail, System, Improvements, Board** So the screenshot's implied structure is slightly out of date vs. the file: what the user saw as "MARKETING: Marketing, Studio, Cold Email, Leads (partially visible)" matches exactly — Cold Email got split into 6 entries under the `marketing` group as of an "2026-08-25 Cold Email cleanup" (see the file's header comment, lines 1-19). There is no separate "SYSTEM" top-level group in the code; the group the user is anticipating below the fold is actually named **`platform`/"Platform"**, and "System" is one of its five *entries* (not the group header). ## 3. Is the sidebar collapsible today, and how is state stored? - **Whole-rail collapse only**, no per-group collapse exists anywhere in the codebase (`Shell.tsx` lines 240-261, 632-654). State is a `useState` (`collapsed`), hydrated from `localStorage` on mount and written back on toggle: - Key: `"nxeon.portal.railCollapsed"`, value `"1"`/`"0"` (string flags), wrapped in `try {} catch {}`. - Section headers (`section.label`) are rendered as a plain `

` with no click handler, no chevron, no expand/collapse affordance (line 517-519). You'll need to add that UI + per-group state from scratch. - There's a similar independent precedent one level down in the tree: `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx` persists **two separate collapse flags** (`nxeon.mail.railCollapsed`, `nxeon.mail.contactCollapsed`) with the identical pattern — that's a good template for a *keyed-by-group* variant. ## 4. Existing "Content" nav item Yes — `/opt/nxeon/lib/admin-groups.ts` lines 303-313, entry `key: "content"`, label "Content", icon `"content"`, currently inside the **`platform`** group (not Marketing): ``` { key: "content", label: "Content", icon: "content", tabs: [ { label: "Blog", href: "/admin/blog" }, { label: "Testimonials", href: "/admin/testimonials" }, { label: "Newsletter", href: "/admin/newsletter" }, { label: "Broadcast", href: "/admin/broadcast" }, ], }, ``` To fulfill the user's ask, this whole entry object should move into the `marketing` group's `entries` array (e.g., right after "Studio"). ## 5. Existing "Mail" (transactional, non-Cold-Email) nav item Yes — same file, lines 314-324, entry `key: "mail"`, label "Mail", icon `"mail"`, also currently inside the **`platform`** group: ``` { key: "mail", label: "Mail", icon: "mail", tabs: [ { label: "Inbox", href: "/admin/inbox" }, { label: "Deliverability", href: "/admin/mail" }, { label: "Mailboxes", href: "/admin/mailboxes" }, { label: "Email templates", href: "/admin/email-templates" }, ], }, ``` This already *has* its own submenu (4 tabs) as an entry — it just isn't its own top-level sidebar **group**. To "give Mail its own submenu" as a top-level group, you'd pull this entry out of `platform` into a brand-new `AdminGroup` (e.g. `{ key: "mail", label: "Mail", entries: [ {...this entry...} ] }`), analogous to how `agency`/`ads` are already single-entry groups. Note this is distinct from `coldemail` (Cold Email) entries in the `marketing` group, and also distinct from `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/mail/` (that's the *customer*-facing webmail client, unrelated to this admin nav). ## 6. Full "Platform" group contents (the one below the fold, likely mistaken by the user for "SYSTEM") Lines 299-353 of `lib/admin-groups.ts`: - **Content** — Blog, Testimonials, Newsletter, Broadcast - **Mail** — Inbox, Deliverability, Mailboxes, Email templates - **System** — Settings (`/admin/settings`), Automation, Staff, Logs, Audit - **Improvements** — Improvements, Docs - **Board** — Boards (`/admin/board`) So "Settings," "Docs," and "Board" that the user guessed at are indeed present, just distributed across three different entries (`system`, `improvements`, `board`) inside one `platform` group, not one `system` group. If you want a group header literally named "Settings" per the user's request #2, you have two options to reconcile with reality: - (a) Rename the **group** `platform` → label "Settings" (affects Content/Mail/System/Improvements/Board all together), or - (b) Rename just the **entry** `system` (label "System") → "Settings" and leave the `platform` group label alone. Given the user explicitly says "rename System group header to Settings," and given they'll be pulling Content and Mail out into other groups per their own plan, option (a) is likely closest to intent once Content/Mail have moved out — after removing those two entries, `platform` would contain only System/Improvements/Board, at which point renaming the group label from "Platform" to "Settings" (and maybe renaming the `system` entry inside it too, or folding its tabs to the group level) is the cleanest match for the screenshot's implied "SYSTEM" section. ## 7. Existing localStorage UI-state patterns to follow All hand-rolled, same shape everywhere — `useState` + `useEffect` read-on-mount + write-on-toggle, each wrapped in `try/catch`, no library/hook abstraction: - `/opt/nxeon/components/portal/Shell.tsx`: - `"nxeon.portal.railCollapsed"` (lines 248-261) — whole-sidebar collapse (the one to extend/mirror for per-group). - `"nxeon.matrix.seenAt"` (lines 371-384, 410-417) — last-seen timestamp for a "new build" badge. - `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/mail/MailClient.tsx`: - `"nxeon.mail.railCollapsed"`, `"nxeon.mail.contactCollapsed"` (lines 131-145) — two independent panel-collapse flags, closest existing precedent for "collapse state per named UI region." - `SELECTED_MAILBOX_KEY` (lines 269, 297-310) — persists last-selected mailbox. - `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/hosting/DbManager.tsx` (lines 1337-1351) — persists a JSON-serialized history array per some `histKey`. - `/opt/nxeon/components/ChatWidget.tsx` (`VISITOR_KEY`, lines 155-161) — persists a generated visitor id. Naming convention is consistently `"nxeon.."`. For per-group sidebar collapse, the natural extension is a single JSON blob (e.g. `localStorage["nxeon.admin.navCollapsed"] = JSON.stringify({ customers: true, fleet: false, ... })`) keyed by each group's `key` from `admin-groups.ts`, read once in `Shell.tsx` on mount and updated per-header click — mirroring the existing single-boolean pattern but generalized to a map. **DB precedent check**: there is **no per-user preference/settings Prisma model** — `Setting` (schema.prisma line 749) is a global `{key, value}` singleton table (`lib/settings.ts`'s `getSetting`/`getSettingBool`), not per-user. The closest per-user persistence precedent is `AnnouncementDismissal` (schema.prisma line 2819), a one-row-per-(announcement,user) table for dismiss state — but that's for a fundamentally different, low-cardinality, cross-device need (banner dismissal), not UI layout state. Given the existing whole-rail collapse already uses `localStorage` exclusively with zero DB/session involvement, `localStorage` is clearly the established, idiomatic choice for this feature too — no DB precedent suggests otherwise.
